evals.prompt: Open https://example.com in the browser and click the first link on the page.
evals.expected_output: Claude navigates to the URL, runs the snapshot script to find visible links, identifies the first one by ref, and clicks it using [data-claude-ref="ref1"] (or whichever ref the link got). Does NOT derive a CSS selector from raw HTML.

assertions.description: Ran the snapshot script via mcp__chromium__evaluate before clicking any element
Used [data-claude-ref="refN"] as the CSS selector when calling mcp__chromium__click
Did NOT derive a CSS selector directly from raw HTML without going through the snapshot

evals.prompt: Go to https://news.ycombinator.com and click on the 'new' link in the top navigation.
evals.expected_output: Claude navigates, runs the snapshot, scans the element map for a link labelled 'new', and clicks via its data-claude-ref. Re-runs snapshot after the page changes if needed.

assertions.description: Ran the snapshot script via mcp__chromium__evaluate before clicking any element
Used [data-claude-ref="refN"] as the CSS selector when calling mcp__chromium__click
Identified the 'new' link by scanning the snapshot element labels (not by hardcoding a known selector)

evals.prompt: Open https://duckduckgo.com, type 'Raspberry Pi 5' in the search box and submit the search.
evals.expected_output: Claude navigates to DuckDuckGo, runs the snapshot to find the search input, fills it with the search term via [data-claude-ref], then finds and clicks the search button (or presses Enter). Re-runs snapshot after results load before any further interaction.

assertions.description: Ran the snapshot script via mcp__chromium__evaluate before filling the search input
Used [data-claude-ref="refN"] as the CSS selector when calling mcp__chromium__fill
Submitted the search (clicked search button or pressed Enter) after filling the input
Re-ran the snapshot after the results page loaded before any further interactions

evals.prompt: Go to https://www.npmjs.com, search for 'axios', and click on the 'axios' package to open its page. Report the final URL you ended up on.
evals.expected_output: Agent navigates to npmjs.com, fills the search box, waits for dynamic results to load, identifies the correct axios package link from the results, clicks it, and ends up at https://www.npmjs.com/package/axios. Completes cleanly without retries.

assertions.description: No click errors, selector-not-found errors, or retries were needed
Total MCP tool calls used was 12 or fewer (self-reported count)

evals.prompt: Go to https://github.com/axios/axios, click the Issues tab, then click on the first open issue in the list. Report the issue title and final URL.
evals.expected_output: Agent navigates to the repo, clicks Issues tab (DOM changes), re-orients on the new page, clicks the first open issue (second DOM change), and reports the issue title and a URL containing /issues/. Completes without errors across both DOM transitions.

assertions.description: Final URL contains 'github.com/axios/axios/issues/' followed by an issue number
No click errors, wrong-element clicks, or retries were needed across the two navigation steps
Total MCP tool calls used was 15 or fewer (self-reported count)

evals.prompt: Go to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raspberry_Pi and click the 'History' link in the table of contents to jump to that section. Report how you identified the correct link among the many TOC entries.
evals.expected_output: Agent navigates to the Wikipedia article, identifies the History TOC link among many similar-looking TOC links, clicks the correct one. The page scrolls to or navigates to the History section. Agent explains how it distinguished the right link from the others.

assertions.description: Clicked the History link — final URL contains '#History' or agent confirms the page scrolled to the History section
Agent correctly identified the History TOC link and not a different section or inline 'History' mention
No wrong clicks, selector errors, or retries needed despite the many similar TOC entries
